Package com.egradx.auth.web

Class EgradxAuthExceptionHandler

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.core.web.EgradxExceptionHandlerSupport
com.egradx.auth.web.EgradxAuthExceptionHandler
@Order(-2147483648) @RestControllerAdvice(assignableTypes={EgradxAuthController.class,EgradxOrganizationController.class,EgradxMyOrganizationController.class,EgradxPermissionController.class,EgradxMyProfileController.class,EgradxMemberProfileController.class,EgradxOrganizationMemberProfileController.class,EgradxPasswordController.class,EgradxMyAccountController.class,EgradxInvitationController.class}) public class EgradxAuthExceptionHandler extends EgradxExceptionHandlerSupport
Scoped to just this module's own controllers (assignableTypes) rather than global, so it doesn't intercept exceptions from unrelated controllers in the host app.

The core exceptions and Spring's request errors are answered by EgradxExceptionHandlerSupport, which keeps an exception's own code (EgradxAuthErrorCodes) over the generic one for its status: that is what lets a client tell "wrong password" from "organization suspended", both 401s. What is auth's own is here.

Ordered first. A host application's own unscoped advice handling the same exception types — OIM's GlobalExceptionHandler handles ValidationException and AccessDeniedException — would otherwise win or lose by registration order, and when it won, this module's routes lost the 401 for an ended session and the details of ORG_SELECTION_REQUIRED. Being scoped to this module's controllers, going first cannot affect anyone else's.
